To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of d- amphetamine and cocaine on accuracy were greater in the learning component than in the performance component, but the effects of d -amphetamine on accuracy in the learning component did not occur until the response chain was well established.

d-amphetamine and, to a lesser extent, cocaine, disrupt the performance of response chains that are learned in a component of a multiple fixed-ratio schedule in which the discriminative stimuli are present, but that this disruption is less pronounced when the response chain has been learned in a component in which the discriminable stimuli are absent, or in a component in a multiple fixed-ratios schedule in which the reinforcers are delivered at a higher rate.

both d-amphetamine and the cocaine were disruptive to the acquisition and performance (but not necessarily the performance of a response chain that had already been acquired) of a response chain in monkeys.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dextroamphetamine and cocaine on the behavior of monkeys in response chain schedules.
the effects of dextroamphetamine and cocaine on the behavior of monkeys performing a multiple schedule of response chains.
the analysis of the behavioral effects of drugs in a multiple schedule of response chain acquisition and performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

both drugs disrupted the behavior in a manner that was consistent with the hypothesis that they impaired the acquisition of new stimulus-response associations and that this impairment was related to the relatively low rate of reinforcement in the learning component.

the effects of both d-amphetamine and of cocaine on response chains in monkeys are complex, and that the effects are related to the specific experimental conditions under which the behavior is measured.
both d-amphetamine and, especially, cocaine have disruptive effects on the acquisition and/or performance of response chains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

d-amphetamine and/or cocaine disrupts behavior in the learning and performance components of a multiple schedule when the drugs are administered prior to the session, and that this disruption may be attenuated when the drug is given after the response chain has been acquired.
the disruptive effects of d-amph and cocaine on behavior in a response-chain task are related to the strength of the stimuli controlling behavior and the rate of reinforcement.
the disruptive effects of cocaine and amphetamine are greater when the behavior is less well established, and that the effects of these drugs are attenuated by increasing the rate of reinforcement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of drugs on behavior depend on the nature of the behavioral processes involved.
drug effects on behavior are highly dependent on task parameters.
the effects of drugs on the behavior of monkeys can be quite different
